author: ValWood
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**


GO:0045732 | positive regulation of protein catabolic process | IBA with P54368 , MGI:109492 , 3219 , MGI:109433 , PTN001616256 , MGI:1858170

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC577.14c

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

I think I get why people have made this annotation, because 
this enzyme, when active, is an inhibitor of polyamine synthesis.
However, it is controlled by polyamine levels via a +1 ribosomal frameshift.

The enzyme is activated by polyamine levels  which allow the frameshift to produce a valid translation.
I guess the active  frameshift would normally result in degradation of the protein (but this isn't the activity of the inhibitor itself, it is just the upstream switch to regulate it)

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).

body: Annotation removed. We have quite a few BP annotations for this family, but, in my opinion, none that really fits to the actual role of those proteins.
